items.title: Music industry group warns Australia against weakening AI copyright rules
items.summary: The International Federation of the Phonographic Industry warned that weakening copyright protections to aid AI companies would be “ridiculous and dangerous,” The Guardian reported. IFPI CEO Victoria Oakley argued that a single safe harbour would let AI firms train on music from anywhere, and said the group is watching Australia’s response to big tech demands.
items.comment: Australia’s decision may influence whether other countries treat AI training as a fair-use or licensing matter.

items.title: US midterms put AI data centers and tech political influence under scrutiny
items.summary: TechCrunch’s Equity podcast reported that voters backed restrictions or moratoriums on data centers in many local ballot measures and elected officials, including Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, who campaigned on restricting them. A Guardian opinion piece said dozens of measures calling for limits on data-center expansion passed and argued the midterms signaled a political backlash against AI infrastructure and tech leaders.
items.comment: The results may slow permitting and reshape AI infrastructure politics, though the practical impact remains uncertain.

items.title: Nvidia CEO reportedly targeted in Chinese intelligence memo
items.summary: TechCrunch, citing New York Times and Financial Times reports, said a U.S. intelligence memo claimed China’s Ministry of State Security recruited Singapore-based executive Alice Huang to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang; the memo also reportedly alleged a romantic relationship. An Nvidia spokesperson told the NYT that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual” and that the company does not share classified information with customers.
items.comment: The allegations are unproven and may intensify scrutiny of contacts between chip executives and Chinese firms.

items.title: UK public bodies face ‘AI clog’ of chatbot-generated complaints
items.summary: The Guardian reported that MPs’ offices, local authorities, courts, schools and other UK public bodies are receiving mounting volumes of AI-generated complaints, requests and legal challenges. A senior caseworker said half the emails her office receives are some form of AI, while researchers described the practice as “agentic flooding.”
items.comment: Cheap generative tools may shift administrative costs onto public institutions, making verification and triage a growing concern.

items.title: AI-exposed vulnerabilities frame a wider cyberattack warning
items.summary: The Guardian described recent cyber incidents including attacks on internet-connected refrigeration units, a $6.3bn Binance heist and a fake nuclear-strike alert in Ukraine. It cited the UK NCSC chief warning of the “foothills” of a new hacking landscape and noted that OpenAI technology helped discover a PHP flaw, while experts debated how much AI is changing the threat.
items.comment: AI’s role in vulnerability discovery may cut both ways, aiding defenders and attackers; the scale of the shift is still uncertain.

items.title: World models gain ground in robotics, cars and games
items.summary: WIRED explained that world models use visual inputs to predict future visual states and simulate physics, unlike text-based large language models. Niantic Spatial, Odyssey, Wayve and Tencent are among those using or investing in the approach for robotics, driverless cars and games, with Niantic drawing on data from Pokémon Go scans.
items.comment: World models may become a key training layer for physical AI, but near-term impact depends on data and simulation fidelity.

items.title: NYT Cooking tests AI recipe modifier in iOS beta
items.summary: WIRED reported that The New York Times is testing an iOS-only beta feature that lets Cooking subscribers use AI to modify recipes, following earlier AI-assisted recipe scaling and measurement conversion. The tool can adapt recipes to available equipment, such as pans, and highlights changes in red-orange text; the rollout drew angry subscriber comments.
items.comment: Consumer patience with AI features in trusted content products may be limited, even when the tool works well.

items.title: MOSS-Live brings full-duplex speech and background tools to real-time agents
items.summary: A Hugging Face blog post introduced MOSS-Live, a full-duplex real-time interaction system that listens and speaks simultaneously, handles interruptions, incorporates live camera or screen input, and runs research or tool use in the background. The post links to GitHub, a live demo and API documentation.
items.comment: Full-duplex interaction may make voice agents feel more natural, though latency and turn-taking remain key tests.

items.title: A developer’s case for leaving Claude Code for Pi
items.summary: In an author’s view post shared on Hacker News, a longtime Claude Code user said accumulated frustrations led them to switch their main coding harness to Pi. The author cited single-session IDE integration, issues with the official VS Code extension and feature churn, and noted that Anthropic announced AGENTS.md support in Claude Code a day after the decision.
items.comment: Developer tooling loyalty may hinge on workflow details and stability as much as raw model quality.

items.title: Llama-modchip claims 284B DeepSeek model on 64GB RAM without GPU
items.summary: The llama-modchip GitHub repository, shared on Hacker News, is titled “284B DeepSeek on 64GB RAM, no GPU,” claiming a way to run a large DeepSeek model on 64GB of RAM without a GPU. The Hacker News submission links to the repository for discussion.
items.comment: Independent benchmarks may be needed to assess whether the approach is practical.
